candidates.reason: Fast baseline that handles mixed numeric and high‑cardinality categorical features (label‑encoded) without requiring scaling. The dataset is small (2.6K rows) and highly imbalanced (On‑site 92%, Remote 8%, Hybrid <1%), so using class_weight='balanced' gives a quick performance floor.

Gradient‑boosted trees excel on tabular data with many categorical columns (even when label‑encoded) and can capture non‑linear patterns observed in the EDA. With only 2.6K rows, XGBoost trains quickly and provides stronger predictive power than the baseline.

LightGBM is another efficient tree‑boosting implementation that works well with high‑cardinality categorical features and small‑to‑medium datasets. It often outperforms XGBoost on speed while delivering comparable accuracy, making it a solid third candidate.

notes: Logistic Regression excluded: label‑encoded high‑cardinality categorical columns introduce artificial ordinal relationships; also requires careful class weighting for the severe imbalance.
SVM (rbf/linear) excluded: O(n^2) complexity is unnecessary for 2.6K rows and performance degrades with many label‑encoded categories.
Neural Network excluded: dataset <5K rows, deep learning would overfit and exceed the quick‑standard time budget.
